## Evidence in one view

::: {.hub-current-state-facts}
- **Registered evidence:** 11 experiment families; 98 registered systems; 16 authored studies; 1 promoted development system.
- **Artifact custody:** 3 complete / 34 receipt-only / 18 report snapshots / 43 blockers.
- **Evidence boundary:** No hidden-test evidence is available.
:::

<h3 id="research-theme-map-title">Studies by method family</h3>

<p class="hub-visual-explanation">This is a presentation-only method-family map, not a canonical taxonomy. It groups every authored study exactly once in a fixed newcomer reading order. Study status vocabulary: Planned, Running, and Concluded.</p>
<div class="hub-theme-reading-map">
<section class="hub-reading-theme" data-method-family="query-baselines-and-neighbors" data-reading-theme="query-baselines-and-neighbors"><h4>Query baselines and neighbors</h4><p class="hub-method-purpose"><strong>Purpose:</strong> Use historical requests to establish a query-only control before adding candidate-side evidence.</p><p class="hub-method-answer"><strong>Working answer:</strong> Dense query neighbors remain the stable query-only control; tested cluster aggregation did not replace it.</p><p class="hub-method-strongest"><strong>Strongest canonical study:</strong> <a href="../studies/dense-query-knn.qmd">Dense query nearest-neighbor retrieval</a> (Concluded)</p><p class="hub-method-open-question"><strong>Open question:</strong> Which request patterns need evidence beyond similar historical queries?</p><p class="hub-method-next-test"><strong>Next valid test:</strong> <a href="../generated/ideas/semantic-failure-clusters.qmd">Semantic failure clusters</a></p><ol>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/query-controls.qmd">Simple query controls</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/dense-query-knn.qmd">Dense query nearest-neighbor retrieval</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/query-cluster-aggregation.qmd">Query-cluster aggregation</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
</ol></section>
<section class="hub-reading-theme" data-method-family="candidate-labels-and-learned-scorers" data-reading-theme="candidate-labels-and-learned-scorers"><h4>Candidate labels and learned scorers</h4><p class="hub-method-purpose"><strong>Purpose:</strong> Use candidate labels as a lightweight clue about fit, and test learned scorers only under a comparable protocol.</p><p class="hub-method-answer"><strong>Working answer:</strong> Contextual E5 remains a control; the tested learned-scorer pilots are not reusable in their tested forms.</p><p class="hub-method-strongest"><strong>Strongest canonical study:</strong> <a href="../studies/candidate-label-matching.qmd">Candidate label matching</a> (Concluded)</p><p class="hub-method-open-question"><strong>Open question:</strong> Can a redesigned learned scorer improve without inheriting the pilots&#x27; restricted or invalid scope?</p><p class="hub-method-next-test"><strong>Next valid test:</strong> <a href="../generated/ideas/semantic-failure-clusters.qmd">Semantic failure clusters</a></p><ol>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/candidate-label-matching.qmd">Candidate label matching</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/label-ranker-pilots.qmd">Label-ranker feasibility pilots</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
</ol></section>
<section class="hub-reading-theme" data-method-family="candidate-profiles-and-fusion" data-reading-theme="candidate-profiles-and-fusion"><h4>Candidate profiles and fusion</h4><p class="hub-method-purpose"><strong>Purpose:</strong> Combine qrel-free candidate profiles with a frozen query control to express complementary candidate-side evidence.</p><p class="hub-method-answer"><strong>Working answer:</strong> Equal dense/profile fusion is the current promoted development direction; alternative weighting is diagnostic only.</p><p class="hub-method-strongest"><strong>Strongest canonical study:</strong> <a href="../studies/semantic-profiles.qmd">Candidate semantic profiles</a> (Concluded)</p><p class="hub-method-open-question"><strong>Open question:</strong> Does the promoted direction generalize when the evaluation protocol is frozen for unseen queries?</p><p class="hub-method-next-test"><strong>Next valid test:</strong> <a href="../generated/ideas/semantic-failure-clusters.qmd">Semantic failure clusters</a></p><ol>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/behavior-profile.qmd">Discovery behavior profile</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/multiresolution-profiles.qmd">Multiresolution candidate profiles</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/semantic-profiles.qmd">Candidate semantic profiles</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
</ol></section>
<section class="hub-reading-theme" data-method-family="direct-response-evidence" data-reading-theme="direct-response-evidence"><h4>Direct response evidence</h4><p class="hub-method-purpose"><strong>Purpose:</strong> Compare bounded candidate-response evidence with the control without disclosing response content.</p><p class="hub-method-answer"><strong>Working answer:</strong> The tested lexical and source-alignment response routes did not displace the control in their tested forms.</p><p class="hub-method-strongest"><strong>Strongest canonical study:</strong> <a href="../studies/response-retrieval.qmd">Lexical response retrieval</a> (Concluded)</p><p class="hub-method-open-question"><strong>Open question:</strong> What privacy-safe response signal can add evidence where both promoted components have no top-ten signal?</p><p class="hub-method-next-test"><strong>Next valid test:</strong> <a href="../generated/ideas/failure-aware-fusion.qmd">Failure-aware evidence fusion</a></p><ol>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/response-retrieval.qmd">Lexical response retrieval</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/response-volume-normalization.qmd">Response-volume normalization</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/source-query-first.qmd">Source-query-first response evidence</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
</ol></section>
<section class="hub-reading-theme" data-method-family="references-and-bounded-refinement" data-reading-theme="references-and-bounded-refinement"><h4>References and bounded refinement</h4><p class="hub-method-purpose"><strong>Purpose:</strong> Use reviewed generated references and bounded refinement as separate evidence routes, not registered ranking rows.</p><p class="hub-method-answer"><strong>Working answer:</strong> A reviewed reference default is useful, while the E5 follow-up remains informational, outside the ledger, and unpromoted.</p><p class="hub-method-strongest"><strong>Strongest canonical study:</strong> <a href="../studies/four-model-reference-review.qmd">Four-model reference-answer review</a> (Concluded)</p><p class="hub-method-open-question"><strong>Open question:</strong> When is generated reference evidence reliable enough to influence a frozen ranking test?</p><p class="hub-method-next-test"><strong>Next valid test:</strong> <a href="../generated/ideas/reference-review-trigger.qmd">Reference review trigger</a></p><ol>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/four-model-reference-review.qmd">Four-model reference-answer review</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/e5-raw-response-refinement.qmd">E5 raw-response refinement</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
</ol></section>
<section class="hub-reading-theme" data-method-family="reliability-failures-and-readiness" data-reading-theme="reliability-failures-and-readiness"><h4>Reliability, failures, and readiness</h4><p class="hub-method-purpose"><strong>Purpose:</strong> Use audits and failure diagnoses to identify when a ranking signal needs a new test, a safeguard, or a stop decision.</p><p class="hub-method-answer"><strong>Working answer:</strong> Known failures show both fusion dilution and missing component signal; audits do not estimate hidden-test prevalence.</p><p class="hub-method-strongest"><strong>Strongest canonical study:</strong> <a href="../studies/sparse-failure-analogue-diagnosis.qmd">Sparse-failure analogue diagnosis</a> (Concluded)</p><p class="hub-method-open-question"><strong>Open question:</strong> Which failure mechanisms repeat under a frozen, privacy-safe evaluation boundary?</p><p class="hub-method-next-test"><strong>Next valid test:</strong> <a href="../generated/ideas/semantic-failure-clusters.qmd">Semantic failure clusters</a></p><ol>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/gemini-grounding-failure-review.qmd">Gemini grounding failure review</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/grounded-data-quality-audit.qmd">Grounded reference data-quality audit</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
<li data-study-status="concluded"><a href="../studies/sparse-failure-analogue-diagnosis.qmd">Sparse-failure analogue diagnosis</a><span class="hub-study-status">Concluded</span></li>
</ol></section>

## Canonical research-theme answers

<div class="hub-canonical-theme-cards">
<section class="hub-canonical-theme" data-canonical-theme="candidate-evidence">
<h3>Candidate evidence</h3>
<p><strong>Current working answer:</strong> Candidate semantic profiles improved development ranking in fusion, but generalization and artifact custody remain unresolved.</p>
<p><strong>Strongest canonical evidence:</strong> The canonical semantic-profiles study supports equal dense/profile fusion as the promoted development direction while keeping higher-scoring weighting variants diagnostic.</p>
<ul class="hub-theme-evidence-refs">
<li><code class="hub-path">reports/trec_2026_experiment_ledger.md</code></li>
<li><code class="hub-path">reports/trec_2026_candidate_semantic_profiles_results.json</code></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Confidence and boundary:</strong> Moderate confidence. Development-only evidence; diagnostic variants and incomplete construction artifacts do not establish hidden-test gains.</p>
<p><strong>Open question:</strong> Will the frozen dense/profile direction generalize to unseen queries once the pre-test protocol and artifact custody are complete?</p>
<p><strong>First linked next test:</strong> <a href="../generated/ideas/semantic-failure-clusters.qmd">Semantic failure clusters</a>: State a falsifiable hypothesis and evaluation boundary for the clustering test. (1 remaining)</p>
</section>
<section class="hub-canonical-theme" data-canonical-theme="evidence-reliability">
<h3>Evidence reliability</h3>
<p><strong>Current working answer:</strong> Known failures cluster around ambiguity, evidence custody, and scope changes; selective review is warranted but no complete reliability predictor exists.</p>
<p><strong>Strongest canonical evidence:</strong> The grounding-failure review and data-quality audit identify useful safeguards, but neither establishes a population-wide reliability rate.</p>
<ul class="hub-theme-evidence-refs">
<li><code class="hub-path">reports/trec_2026_four_model_reference_review_2026-07-21.md</code></li>
<li><code class="hub-path">reports/trec_2026_grounded_data_quality_audit_2026-07-23.md</code></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Confidence and boundary:</strong> Low confidence. Audits use purposive or known-failure samples and do not estimate hidden-test prevalence.</p>
<p><strong>Open question:</strong> Which reproducible trigger can route only genuinely unreliable generated evidence to grounding or review?</p>
<p><strong>First linked next test:</strong> <a href="../generated/ideas/failure-aware-fusion.qmd">Failure-aware evidence fusion</a>: Define and freeze the reliability signal, fallback, and artifact plan. (4 remaining)</p>
</section>
<section class="hub-canonical-theme" data-canonical-theme="query-only-routing">
<h3>Query-only routing</h3>
<p><strong>Current working answer:</strong> Dense query neighbors remain the stable control, while tested cluster aggregations have not displaced them.</p>
<p><strong>Strongest canonical evidence:</strong> The dense-query-nearest-neighbor study establishes dense_nested as the frozen query-only control, while tested cluster aggregations did not displace it.</p>
<ul class="hub-theme-evidence-refs">
<li><code class="hub-path">reports/trec_2026_experiment_ledger.md</code></li>
<li><code class="hub-path">reports/trec_2026_dense_query_knn_results.json</code></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Confidence and boundary:</strong> Moderate confidence. Development-only evidence with repeated tuning on the same queries; hidden-test transfer is unknown.</p>
<p><strong>Open question:</strong> Which unseen-query patterns require candidate-side or response-derived evidence beyond the dense query control?</p>
<p><strong>First linked next test:</strong> <a href="../generated/ideas/semantic-failure-clusters.qmd">Semantic failure clusters</a>: State a falsifiable hypothesis and evaluation boundary for the clustering test. (1 remaining)</p>
</section>
<section class="hub-canonical-theme" data-canonical-theme="responses-references">
<h3>Responses and references</h3>
<p><strong>Current working answer:</strong> Direct lexical response retrieval underperformed, while reference-based and bounded refinement paths provide separate diagnostic evidence.</p>
<p><strong>Strongest canonical evidence:</strong> The four-model reference review supports a default reference generator, while the completed E5 refinement remains separate informational evidence outside the registered ledger.</p>
<ul class="hub-theme-evidence-refs">
<li><code class="hub-path">reports/trec_2026_experiment_ledger.md</code></li>
<li><code class="hub-path">reports/trec_2026_e5_raw_response_refinement_results.md</code></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Confidence and boundary:</strong> Low confidence. Most ranking evidence is development-only, some response data is private or local, and reference quality varies by case.</p>
<p><strong>Open question:</strong> What privacy-safe response or reference signal can earn a frozen comparison with the dense/profile control?</p>
<p><strong>First linked next test:</strong> <a href="../generated/ideas/failure-aware-fusion.qmd">Failure-aware evidence fusion</a>: Define and freeze the reliability signal, fallback, and artifact plan. (2 remaining)</p>
</section>
</div>

<p class="hub-visual-status"><strong>Status:</strong> Benchmark workflow</p>
<p class="hub-visual-explanation">The system ranks candidate LLMs; it does not answer the request. Construction and evaluation stay separated.</p>
<ol class="hub-map-flow" aria-hidden="true">
<li><strong>New request</strong><span>Receive an unseen request without its relevance labels.</span></li>
<li><strong>Allowed evidence</strong><span>Use frozen query, profile, or response evidence.</span></li>
<li><strong>Rank candidates</strong><span>Score and order all candidate model identifiers.</span></li>
<li><strong>Submit and evaluate</strong><span>Write a TREC run; evaluate only when labels exist.</span></li>
</ol>
